title: Seven Dips in the River
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Big Naaman was a soldier, strong,
with sores from head to toe.
A little servant girl said, “Sir,
the prophet helps; please go!”

[Chorus]
The little things that God asks you
might seem too plain and small.
So do them, and the blessings come,
the biggest of them all.

[Verse 2]
“Wash seven times,” the message said.
“Too easy! Not for me!”
“Just try!” they begged. He dipped and dipped;
seven! Clean as can be!

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Now close your eyes; you’re washed and clean,
the river’s running slow.
Heavenly Father’s close tonight;
small steps will help you grow.

[Chorus]
mood: Splashing music. A light, bouncing sway under the voice, playful enough to count seven dips on, with a little dip-and-rise in each phrase like going under and coming up. The chorus steadies into something plainer and surer, the way a simple task turns out to matter. By the last verse the bounce slows to a gentle rock and sinks low, the river calm and the child clean and drowsy.
